title: Token Pacing and Staleness Lab
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal lab notes exploring how few-shot exemplar freshness + token-pacing strategies interact with short- and long-lived sessions. Trying to capture experiments to reproduce later and sketch an adaptive exemplar-refresh approach for streaming chat endpoints.

Background + motivation:
- Problem: In multi-turn chat and long lived sessions, the exemplars and few-shot context that were helpful early can become stale or actively harmful as the user conversation steers into new subtopics.
- Secondary problem: Naively keeping many exemplars to hedge coverage increases token cost and latency; need selective pacing.
- Goal: find simple heuristics / lightweight policies (no heavy infra changes) that reduce hallucination/regression and token cost while preserving latency SLOs.

Hypotheses:
1) A small rolling exemplar window (~3 items) refreshed on semantic shift reduces topical confusion vs static few-shot sets.
2) Exemplar utility decays roughly exponentially with dialog turns since last match; decay rate depends on domain drift.
3) Token-pacing (interleaving shorter system-level cues + 1 exemplar vs full 3 exemplar block) can maintain quality while lowering cost by ~20-35%.

Experiment matrix (high-level):
- Vars:
  - exemplar set size: 0,1,3,5
  - refresh policy: static, time-based (T=5m,15m), turn-based (every 3 turns), semantic-shift-triggers (embedding-distance>thresh)
  - token-pacing mode: full-block, staggered (partial before user message, rest after), on-demand (only when LM confidence low)
  - model variants: open-7b-quant, open-13b-4bit (bench on Dedicated pool)
- Metrics:
  - QA fidelity / correctness (task specific), BLEU/EM for synthetic sets
  - hallucination rate (manual label on 200 samples)
  - latency P95 (end-to-end tokens-in->tokens-out)
  - tokens-per-session (cost proxy)

Quick results summary (pilot runs 2026-03-03 to 2026-03-08):
- Baseline static-3 exemplars: good early-turn accuracy but degrades after ~6 turns (more contradictory answers). Tokens/session: high.
- Turn-based refresh (every 3 turns) + exemplar size 3: reduced contradiction by ~12% vs static-3; tokens +10% (refresh cost).
- Semantic-shift-trigger (embedding cosine < 0.75 vs last anchor) + exemplar size 3: best tradeoff; contradiction -18%, tokens -22% vs static-3 (because refreshes only when needed).
- Token-pacing staggered: send 1 exemplar in the system prompt and defer others as a lightweight context via truncated summary appended only when LM-confidence low -> latency +5ms, tokens -28%, small drop in factuality (~2 points). Good candidate for budget mode.

Failure modes observed (hand-curated examples):
1) Frequent small-topic hops (user lists many micro-questions) cause embed-distance flip-flops -> too many refreshes. Need hysteresis or minimum time/turn window.
2) Sensitive safety cues: removing certain safety exemplar lines in staggered delivery introduced short-lived policy regressions in 3 samples; must keep safety/system constraints always in the primary system prompt.
3) Exemplars with contradictory internal style (e.g., formal vs casual) confuse role priming when refreshed mid-session; need style-normalization step on candidate exemplars.

Notable raw example (for reproduction):
- Conversation sketch: user starts with "help me debug this SQL" -> exemplar A (SQL-debug fewshot); later user says "now convert to pandas" -> exemplar B (python-pandas fewshot). Static-3 kept SQL examples and LM kept giving SQL-centric suggestions even after multiple clarifying turns. Semantic-refresh swapped in exemplar B and corrected behavior.

Algorithm sketch: exemplar-refresh controller (pseudo):
1) maintain ring buffer of last N user turns (N=20 default) and an "anchor embedding" (weighted avg of most recent user messages).
2) on new user msg: compute cosine(new_emb, anchor_emb). if < THRESH_old - HYSTERESIS then: fetch candidate exemplars filtered by current intent tag -> score by recency/semantic-similarity/style-match -> replace least-relevant exemplar in serving set; update anchor_emb with momentum alpha.
3) throttle: at most 1 refresh per 2 turns or 30s. Always preserve safety/system tokens in primary.

Candidate exemplar scoring (notes):
- Combine: lambda1 * cosine(candidate, recent_user) + lambda2 * recency_score + lambda3 * style_match.
- Style match: simple length + punctuation heuristics + embedding distance to user-turn-style-vector. Simple but cheap.

Experiment log (raw):
- run-2026-03-03-13: open-7b-quant, static-3, test-suite-A (50 dialogs): hallucination 9/50, tokens/session median 420.
- run-2026-03-05-17: open-7b-quant, semishift-thresh0.75, staggered-pacing: hallucination 3/50, tokens/session median 310.
- run-2026-03-07-10: open-13b-4bit, semishift-thresh0.78: latency p95 +18ms vs 7b, hallucination 2/50 but tokens/session 360.

Notes to self / ideas for next mini experiments:
- Try memory-compressed exemplars: replace full exemplars with short micro-summaries (10-20 tokens) that are expanded server-side only when LM-confidence low. Measure tokens & latency costs of expansion.
- Hysteresis tuning: test pair (thresh +- 0.03) and min-refresh intervals 1/2/3/5 turns.
- Explore using LM-internal confidence proxy (logprob delta) vs external heuristic. See MLINF-2143 for earlier notes.
- Add automated sampling hook in Console to mark dialogs with sudden top-1 intent change for labeling.

Prompt templates used (examples):
- System (safety + instructions): "You are an assistant that answers precisely. Always ask clarifying questions before making assumptions. If the user provides code, explain changes in diff-style. KEEP SYSTEM SAFETY LINES (do not remove)."
- Few-shot exemplar example (SQL->pandas case): "Example: User: 'How to convert SELECT... to pandas?' Assistant: 'Use pd.read_sql_query(...) and then df.query(...)' -> short canonical mapping."

Quick TODO checklist:
- [ ] Add gating/hysteresis implementation to exemplar-controller (PR draft).
- [ ] Instrument LM-confidence metric in dedicated logs and add to console dashboard.
- [ ] Create 200 labeled dialogs covering: long-lived sessions, frequent micro-hops, style shifts.
- [ ] Write up short playbook for solutions-eng (one-pager) summarizing token-pacing budget-mode patterns.

References + context links:
- Jira: MLINF-2143 (embedding triggers for exemplar refresh)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rl-infra/pull/981 (initial controller wiring, WIP)
- Confluence draft: Token Pacing Playbook (internal)

Personal reflections (scratch):
- Semantic-trigger approach seems promising for real workloads where topical shifts are sparse. For chatty users with many micro-asks the cost of switching may be higher than benefit; need better detection of micro-hops vs true topic change.
- Keep safety/system unconditionally present. No tradeoffs there.
- Prefer staggered pacing default for free-tier / budget clusters.

Raw notes / ephemeral TODO commands:
- Re-run run-2026-03-05 with a min-refresh delay 2 turns and log which exemplar IDs were evicted.
- Add small synthetic bench that 1) flips topics every turn and 2) sustained single topic for 12 turns to measure false-positive refresh rate.

-- end of scratchpad --
